context.problem_statement: Rewrite a slow query to leverage date-based table partitioning in PostgreSQL. The original unpartitioned table 'sales_all' has 50M rows. (1) Create a RANGE partitioned version 'sales_partitioned' partitioned by month on sale_date. (2) Show the DDL for creating monthly partitions for Jan-Jun 2024. (3) Rewrite the query to ensure partition pruning occurs (verify with EXPLAIN that only relevant partitions are scanned). (4) Show the EXPLAIN difference between scanning 'sales_all' vs 'sales_partitioned' for a 3-month date range query. (5) Implement a DEFAULT partition for out-of-range dates.
context.expert_knowledge: PostgreSQL partition pruning: only executes for queries with WHERE clause on partition key. Use PARTITION BY RANGE (sale_date). Create partitions: CREATE TABLE sales_2024_01 PARTITION OF sales_partitioned FOR VALUES FROM ('2024-01-01') TO ('2024-02-01'). Constraint exclusion must be on (default). Pruning only works when partition key appears directly in WHERE (avoid function wrapping). Attach DEFAULT partition: CREATE TABLE sales_default PARTITION OF sales_partitioned DEFAULT.
